findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "submit_mock_exam" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Submit a timed set from start_mock_exam and get the score report: total, whether it reached the target, score per topic, and the missed problems with worked sol…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_answer, get_progress, get_study_plan · Private data: check_answer, start_mock_exam, submit_mock_exam, reset_progress · Public sink: save_mock_answers, submit_mock_exam · Destructive: get_exam_overview, reset_progress.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_answer, get_progress, get_study_plan · Private data: check_answer, start_mock_exam, submit_mock_exam, reset_progress · Public sink: save_mock_answers, submit_mock_exam · Destructive: get_exam_overview, reset_progress

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
